svg.title: Charge concentrates where a conductor is most sharply curved
svg.desc: (a) On an egg-shaped conductor, identical pairs of charges at the blunt left end and the sharp right end repel with equal forces F, but the component F∥ parallel to the surface is larger at the blunt end, so charges are pushed away from it and toward the sharper end. (b) Computed charge marks and field lines of the charged conductor: the charge, and the field, are densest at the sharply curved right end. (c) Computed field lines of the neutral conductor in an originally uniform field: the induced charge, and the field just outside, are greatest at the sharply curved end.
